races.title: State Assembly, District 27
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brian Pacheco
cands.bio: Fourth-generation Fresno County dairy farmer. Fresno County Supervisor for District 1 since 2015. Previously spent 12 years on the Kerman Unified School District board and was president of the Fresno County Farm Bureau. Democratic nominee for Assembly District 27.

endorsements.text: Speaker of the Assembly Robert Rivas and Assemblymember Esmeralda Soria are quoted endorsing him on his campaign site.

Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521 and California Young Democrats.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or the year he came to California beyond his family's long farming roots in the Valley. We found no documented votes or actions as a county supervisor, such as county budget, land-use or development decisions. We found no stated positions on data centers or development limits, and none on immigration, guns, abortion, school choice, or restrictions on investor or foreign land buyers. His campaign site mentions building more affordable housing but gives no specifics. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. No news reporting or controversies were available to review.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was raised on his family's dairy farm and graduated from Kerman High School, and describes him as a fourth-generation Valley farmer, but it does not give a birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Fresno County Supervisor (District 1) since 2015, 12 years on the Kerman Unified School District board, and a working dairy farmer. Past president of the Fresno County Farm Bureau and former chairman of California Dairies, Inc. Holds a UC Davis agricultural economics degree.
qual.why: Eleven years in county elected office, which sets the county budget, plus a dozen years of school board service and business and cooperative leadership. He has not served in a state legislature, so the score falls short of the top band.

cands.name: Mike Murphy
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 27 in 2026. He finished first in the June 2 primary with 43.4% and lost the November 3 general election to Democrat Brian Pacheco. The sources I could read give no other biographical details.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these endorsements and voter-guide recommendations: Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Mike Murphy was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no information on his occupation, work history or any elected office. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign website text, interviews or questionnaires stating his positions. We found no documented actions or statements on data centers, development, property taxes, housing, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no reporting on controversies or foreign ties.
